messages:
marta: Heads-up — noticed a ~3x spike in fncall.schema_rejects starting 23:42 UTC after we rolled the debounce change to the validator. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/fncall-errors ?orgId=1
canary-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: fncall.schema_rejects rate > threshold (3m avg) for route: /invoke/tool (svc-id=svc-fn-06)
devon: Is this global or hitting a single customer/route?
marta: Mostly one route + a burst from eu-west. 80% of rejects are "missing_required_field" on tool_response.object
sam: Can you paste the example payload that's failing? Want to check if it's the validator change tightening unions
marta: example (redacted):
```
{"tool": "send_email", "response": {"to": null, "body": "..."}}
```
li: ah yeah — the new debounce also flipped on strict enum + nonnull enforcement for streaming fragments. We probably started rejecting partial fragments that used `null` for optional subfields
nisha: Is this causing billing/regression or just noise?
marta: It is incrementing reject counters which are used by quota attribution. Some customers saw a brief 429-ish flow because downstream fallback to degen route triggered quota pathing.
devon: That's bad if users get charged or see increased latency. We should avoid changing billing semantics with a validation tweak.
sam: Agreed. Options: 1) revert debounce, 2) add permissive soft-validate mode per-route, 3) adapt routing to send rejects to a non-billable sample pipeline while we triage
li: I can sketch a quick permissive flag: `fncall.validation.mode = [strict|soft|lenient]` exposed to Console per-route. Soft emits metric tag `validation.soft=true` and doesn't increment chargeable reject counters
marta: Love that. From an ops POV we also need better dashboard labels: show reject-reason, route_id, validation_mode, and whether fallback route was used
canary-bot: New incident created: INC-2026-fncall-schema-spike — assigned to eng-platform; severity: P2
nisha: For short-term mitigation can we route rejects->degen in a non-billable queue? We already have `degen-debug` route for sampling
devon: Doable. But need to ensure console quota UI doesn't surface this as customer-facing billing spike. We can add a temporary mapping: `metric.label.billed = false` for metrics with `validation.soft=true` or route `degen-debug`
sam: Quick query we used: `sum(rate(fncall_schema_rejects[5m])) by (route,reason,region)` — shows top reason = missing_required_field, route=/invoke/tool, region=eu-west
li: I'll open a tiny PATCH to the validator to add a soft-validate flag with default=false and add a telemetry tag. Then we can toggle on a per-slice canary (percent of requests) in the routing policy
marta: Timeline? We should avoid a full revert if we can soft-mode it in <2 hrs
li: I can get a PR by EOD and then a quick canary (1%) -> 10% -> 50% rollout plan. Need ops help to patch dashboards and metric mapping
nisha: I'll update the Console: add a short-lived filter in the quota dashboard to exclude `validation.soft=true` and annotate the billing graph with INC-2026
devon: Also add an alert rule suppressed by `validation.soft` so noise doesn't fire post-mitigation
sam: Do we need to backfill telemetry for samples? We should mark recent rejects we decide to reclassify so accounting matches retroactively
isha: Good call — we'll add an ingestion label `reclassify_candidate=true` for the next 6 hours on the sampling collector and a backfill job can re-tag past 1h worth of samples if the final decision is to not bill
marta: OK — action items: li PR soft-validate flag + telemetry tag; nisha patch dashboard + metric mapping; devon set non-billable degen route and alert suppression; sam coordinate backfill/runbook. I'll own comms to customer-success.
li: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4599 — adds flag and tags (draft)
nisha: Dashboard patch: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/fncall-errors?edit=true (I will add columns: reason, mode, billed)
devon: I'll create a routing quickfix and flip to degen-debug for route svc-fn-06, canary at 1% now, watching trace-ids
sam: Thanks — keep updates in this thread. If we see rejects drop after soft-mode toggle we can avoid revert
marta: Update 23:59 UTC: applied soft-mode (1% canary). Reject rate dropped ~60% for the sampled slice. Continuing rollout to 10%
canary-bot: Notice: canary rollout successful at 10% — no errors in trace sampling for new validation flag
marta: Great work. We'll reconvene in 30m to decide full rollout vs. revert.
